environment: Hervey Bay's humpback whale season hits its spring peak as thousands of whales cruise past the Queensland coast
Queensland's big battery and rooftop solar boom keeps pushing the Sunshine State toward its renewable energy targets
science: Australian marine scientists roll out new reef monitoring tech to track coral recovery on the Great Barrier Reef
sports: Finals footy fever grips Brisbane as NRL and AFL finals season kicks into gear with Queensland sides in the mix
stories.overview: Spring has sprung across Queensland with whales breaching offshore, wildflowers popping and warmer days lighting up the Sunshine State

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, it's Monday the seventh of September and mate, spring has well and truly sprung around Queensland. I'm Alex Mercer, and next to me as always is the one and only Jamie. Morning Alex, and morning to all of you tuning in. We've got a ripper show for you today, whales putting on a show off the coast, some clever reef science, footy finals heating up and Sam's got the weather sorted for the week ahead. Reckon we better get into it then, there's a lot of good news to squeeze in before smoko. Let's kick things off with the environment desk, shall we Jamie.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: So Alex, it is peak whale season out at Hervey Bay right now, and the humpbacks are putting on an absolute show as they cruise down the Queensland coast with their calves in tow. Whale watching boats have been packed out and honestly, there's nothing quite like watching a forty tonne animal fling itself out of the water for no reason other than it can. Love that for them honestly, showing off a bit before winter's properly done. Meanwhile back on land, Queensland keeps quietly smashing it on renewables, with big batteries and household solar panels popping up all over the place as the state chases its clean energy targets. It's the sort of steady, unglamorous progress that doesn't always make headlines but it adds up, panel by panel and battery by battery. Good stuff all round for Mother Nature this week.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Right, let's shift over to science, and this one's close to home for us Queenslanders. Marine researchers have been rolling out some clever new monitoring tech out on the Great Barrier Reef, designed to keep a much closer eye on how the coral is bouncing back after all the stress it's copped over the years. It's basically giving scientists a proper health check up on the reef in real time, rather than waiting months to find out how things are tracking. That means quicker decisions and hopefully quicker help for the parts of the reef that need it most. Bit of good old Aussie ingenuity keeping our biggest natural wonder ticking along. Big tick for the boffins on that one.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and morning everyone, Sam here with your south east Queensland outlook. We're settling into a classic spring pattern this week, mostly clear skies, cool mornings down around the mid teens and lovely mild afternoons climbing into the mid to high twenties across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast. Winds should stay fairly light out of the south east, seas are calm for anyone heading out on the water, and there's next to no rain in sight, so it is shaping up as a cracking week for getting outdoors, just don't forget the sunscreen because that spring sun has a bit of bite to it already. Back to you two in the studio.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Righto, sport, and this is my favourite time of year, finals footy is here. Both the NRL and AFL are deep into their finals series now, and there's a real buzz around Brisbane with our local sides right in the thick of the action. You can feel it around town too, pubs are packed, jerseys are out and everyone's got an opinion on who's going all the way this year. Doesn't matter which code you follow, finals time just hits different. Too right, nothing like a bit of September footy to get the blood pumping. Good luck to all the Queensland sides still standing, we'll be cheering you on.
